chapter: Hines 1935-38, Gus Arnheim and Billy Eckstine
title: Playing with Horace Henderson before rejoining Hines
summary: Back in Chicago Budd plays at the Savoy with Horace Henderson, a great arranger now raising horses in Colorado.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: He said, 'So, I'm going to take this position and you guys have been all right, and blah, blah.' So, then, I came back to Chicago, see, and I joined -- re-joined Earl. Now, this was, like, around -- well, before I rejoined Earl, I worked with Horace Henderson in the -- and Horace had just come out of -- Fletcher Henderson's

Henderson's Hillison's brother. And -- and, we were like working in the Savoy, like once or twice a week. And, I joined his band and played with him for a while. And, then, finally, I went back with Earl.
Horace played piano and what a great arranger he was. Beautiful. Incidentally, Horace is living in Denver, Colorado, and he's raising Arabian horses and peacocks. He's got a little farm there.
